content: Stannous fluoride is an anti-cavity, anti-gingivitis, and anti-hypersensitivity mouth rinse that has been approved by the FDA for the prevention of dental decay. It helps prevent gingivitis, controls plaque bacteria, and increases protection against painful tooth sensitivity. A common adverse reaction associated with its use is surface staining of the teeth. For adults and children aged 6 years and older, the product should not be used before mixing with water. It must be used immediately after preparation. To prepare, remove the cap and replace it with the pump. Rotate the spout clockwise to extend it, then depress the pump until the rinse reaches the tip. Dispense the rinse by depressing the pump twice into the provided cup (1/8 oz), then add water to the 1 oz line on the cup and mix well. Swish the rinse vigorously between the teeth for one minute and spit it out. Do not swallow the rinse. Avoid eating or drinking for 30 minutes after rinsing. Children under 12 years of age should be instructed on proper use to minimize swallowing, and supervision is recommended until they can use the product independently. For children under 6 years of age, consult a dentist or doctor. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of stannous fluoride in both adult and pediatric patients. Similarly, there is limited data on contraindications, clinical trial experiences, postmarketing experiences, drug interactions, and its use in specific populations such as pregnant or nursing women, pediatric and geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. There is also no established guidance on its use in immunocompromised patients, specific genders, or racial populations. Warnings include keeping the product out of reach of children, not swallowing the rinse, and seeking medical help or contacting a Poison Control Center immediately if more than the recommended amount is accidentally swallowed. The product should not be used until diluted. Surface staining of the teeth may occur, but these stains are not harmful or permanent and can be removed by a dentist. Adequate tooth brushing may help prevent these stains. There is no FDA guidance on the use of stannous fluoride during pregnancy, labor, delivery, or in nursing mothers. Additionally, there is no information on its pharmacology, including its mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, or nonclinical toxicology. Limited information is available regarding its administration, monitoring, IV compatibility, and overdose management. If overdose or poisoning is suspected, contact the National Poison Help hotline immediately. The product should be stored at controlled room temperature (59°–86°F or 15°–30°C) and protected from freezing. There is no established interaction between stannous fluoride and alcohol, but patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding alcohol use with this medication. Information on brand names, look-alike drug names, and patient counseling is also limited.
